core_obligations: Translate the diagram (proof lines 6719-6736): a diagram in the quotient with a surjective f_2 corresponds to ring maps f_i, elements x, x_1, x_2 of U over A, A_1, A_2 and elements a_1, a_2 of R(A) with the stated compatibility conditions.

Construct the candidate fibre product (proof lines 6738-6752): let a = c(i(a_1), a_2) in R(A); by smoothness of s there is a lift a-tilde in R(A_2) with s(a-tilde) = x_2 and R(f_2)(a-tilde) = a, and t(a-tilde) and x_1 then define an element of U(A_1) x_{U(A)} U(A_2) which by (RS) for U corresponds to an element x_1 x t(a-tilde) of U(A_1 x_A A_2); the claim is that the resulting object over A_1 x_A A_2 makes the displayed square cartesian.

Verify the fibre square (proof lines 6754-6787): the square commutes because of the cocycle relation; given any competing commutative diagram over B, the map on rings must be the pair (g_1, g_2) and, using (RS) for R to write the comparison element as a pair agreeing over A, the commutativity conditions force the pair to be (b_1, c(a-tilde, b_2)), which proves existence and uniqueness and hence (RS) for the quotient.
proof_roadmap: Translate a diagram in the quotient groupoid into explicit ring and element data.
Use smoothness of the source map to lift one arrow and (RS) for the objects to form the candidate fibre product.
Check commutativity and the universal property, using (RS) for the arrows to separate the comparison element into its two components.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the quotient of a smooth groupoid in functors on the category of Artinian algebras by an equivalence relation whose objects and arrows both satisfy (RS) again satisfies (RS) (statement lines 6713-6717). The proof (proof lines 6719-6789) translates a diagram in the quotient into explicit data, uses smoothness of the source map to lift an arrow and (RS) for the objects to build the candidate fibre product, and verifies the universal property using (RS) for the arrows. H3: an original construction of a fibre product in a quotient groupoid with a full universal property check, written out in full.
